answer: Submissions that land within 69 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The comet detector writes to juniper, and opal makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 289 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
